status: Flat-list clipboard controller integrated internally; full editor owner/router and physical clipboard qualification remain open

contracts.implementation: Shared private clipboard controller with explicit base/list facades, fixed private mode and exact adapter-executor queue lease
contracts.selection: Owned hierarchical range and exact bound presentation; actual AST text-block paths, scalar offsets, partial and empty boundary slices
contracts.interchange: Selected plain text separated by LF and escaped paragraph HTML with checked inline wrappers; no list markers, heading ranks or structural rich paste
contracts.cut: Write both representations, confirm cancellation, then submit one list-aware deletion
contracts.paste: Advertised plain text is authoritative; HTML-only uses the unchanged closed paragraph/inline allowlist and reduces to plain text; Rust handles destination list structure
contracts.lifecycle: Queue exclusion, stale-base checks, partial-progress diagnostics, one-use cut/paste echoes and uncertainty without retry are shared with the existing controller
contracts.limits: Existing serialization, HTML admission and command-text/source-paragraph budgets remain unchanged; valid larger list selections can exceed clipboard limits
contracts.legacy: No new shipping exports, package version, durable format or Wasm change

verification.declarationEmission: passed into temporary directory, not shipping dist
verification.browserScope: Real list clipboard controller/queue/adapter/Wasm with native-branded synthetic events and in-memory DataTransfer. Mixed-root copy, backward emoji and cross-item cut, plain/HTML-only multiline paste, empty bullet-item paste, one-use beforeinput/input echoes, unsupported HTML rejection, exact undo and fresh-owner Session V6 redo. Earlier ordinary/composition/toolbar scenarios also rerun.
developmentCorrections: One initial unit expectation used adapterUnavailable for a second attempted paste after uncertain generated selection synchronization. The shared queue correctly fails closed first with queueUnavailable; corrected the expectation and retained the one-call/no-retry assertion.

First browser run passed Chromium/WebKit but Firefox copy left the fixture's supplied transfer empty. Independent constructor probes proved Firefox creates a separate empty event transfer and ignores supplied initial entries. A second run, reading the actual event transfer, passed copy/cut but blocked empty paste. The fixture now seeds and reads the actual event-local transfer. No production event getters or admission were weakened. Final five-run suites pass all three browsers.
